chien-tete-en-bas.name: Downward-Facing Dog
chien-tete-en-bas.summary: A gentle inverted-V inversion that lengthens the whole back body and strengthens the arms and shoulders.

entry: Start on hands and knees, hands slightly ahead of shoulders.
Tuck the toes and lift the hips up and back.
Lengthen the spine, bending the knees as needed.
hold: Press the floor away, shoulders away from the ears.
Let the head hang between the arms.
Let the heels reach down without forcing.
exit: Lower the knees and return to tabletop or Child's Pose.

chien-tete-en-bas.breath: Breathe fully, lengthening the spine on each inhale.

pince-debout.name: Standing Forward Fold
pince-debout.summary: A standing forward bend that stretches the back of the legs and releases the back and neck.
contraindications: Herniated disc or acute low back pain

entry: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Hinge from the hips with a long spine.
Let the torso lower, bending the knees as needed.
hold: Relax the head and neck.
Place hands on the floor, shins or blocks.
Keep weight spread across the whole foot.
exit: Bend the knees and slowly roll up to standing.

pince-debout.breath: Exhale to fold; let each exhale soften you further.

montagne.name: Mountain
montagne.summary: The foundational standing pose that builds alignment, grounding and presence.
contraindications: Dizziness or low blood pressure: stay near support

entry: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart.
Spread weight across the whole foot.
Lengthen the spine, crown of the head rising.
hold: Arms by the sides, shoulders relaxed.
Lightly engage thighs and core.
Keep a steady gaze forward.
exit: Release and move into the next pose.

montagne.breath: Calm, steady breathing through the nose.

facile.name: Easy Pose
facile.summary: A simple cross-legged seat used for breathing, meditation and centering.
contraindications: Knee or hip pain: raise the hips
Low back pain: sit on a cushion

entry: Sit and cross the legs, feet below opposite knees.
Raise the hips on a cushion if needed.
Lengthen the spine above the pelvis.
hold: Hands on knees, shoulders relaxed.
Chin slightly tucked.
Alternate the leg cross from time to time.
exit: Uncross the legs and extend them gently.

facile.breath: Slow, natural breathing with attention on the breath.

quatre-pattes.name: Tabletop
quatre-pattes.summary: A hands-and-knees position with a flat back that serves as the base for many sequences.
contraindications: Wrist pain: use fists or forearms

entry: Come onto hands and knees.
Hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Lengthen the back from head to tailbone.
hold: Press the floor away with the hands.
Lightly engage the belly.
Gaze down, neck long.
exit: Sit back on the heels or move to the next pose.

quatre-pattes.breath: Smooth breathing with a steady back.

savasana.name: Corpse Pose (Savasana)
savasana.summary: A supine relaxation that lets the practice settle and releases the whole body.
contraindications: Late pregnancy: lie on the side
Low back pain: bolster under knees

entry: Lie on the back, legs apart.
Arms by the sides, palms up.
Adjust the neck and close the eyes.
hold: Consciously relax each part of the body.
Let the breath become natural.
Stay 5 to 10 minutes.
exit: Gently move fingers and toes, roll to one side, then sit up.

savasana.breath: Let the breath happen without directing it.

enfant.name: Child's Pose
enfant.summary: A kneeling resting pose with the forehead down that gently stretches the back and invites calm.

entry: Kneel with big toes touching, knees together or apart.
Sit back toward the heels.
Fold forward, forehead on the floor or a prop.
hold: Arms extended forward or alongside the body.
Relax shoulders and jaw.
Feel the breath in the back.
exit: Slowly roll up, one vertebra at a time.

enfant.breath: Breathe slowly, widening the back on the inhale.

fente-haute.name: High Lunge
fente-haute.summary: A standing lunge on the ball of the back foot that strengthens the legs and opens the front of the hip.
contraindications: High blood pressure: keep hands on hips
Balance issues: practice near a wall

entry: From Mountain, take a big step back.
Bend the front knee over the ankle.
Back heel lifted, back leg active.
hold: Hips facing forward, torso upright.
Raise the arms, shoulders relaxed.
Keep a steady gaze ahead.
exit: Place the hands down and step the back foot forward.

fente-haute.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to root through the legs.

fente-basse.name: Low Lunge
fente-basse.summary: A lunge with the back knee down that opens the front of the hips and the chest.
contraindications: Sensitive knee: blanket under the knee
Low back pain: limit the arch

entry: From Downward Dog, step one foot between the hands.
Lower the back knee to the floor.
Front knee over the ankle.
hold: Ease the hips gently forward.
Raise the arms or keep hands on the thigh.
Lengthen the lower back.
exit: Hands down and step back to Dog or tabletop.

fente-basse.breath: Inhale to open the chest, exhale to soften the hip.

palmier.name: Palm Tree
palmier.summary: A standing overhead stretch, often on tiptoes, that lengthens the whole body.

entry: From Mountain, interlace the fingers.
Raise the arms overhead, palms up.
Rise onto the toes if balance allows.
hold: Stretch from feet to fingertips.
Fix the gaze for balance.
exit: Lower the heels and release the arms.

palmier.breath: Inhale to rise, exhale to come down.

wind-release-pose.name: Wind-Relieving Pose
wind-release-pose.summary: A supine pose hugging the knees to the chest that massages the abdomen and releases the low back.

entry: Lie on the back.
Draw one or both knees toward the chest.
Wrap the arms around the shins.
hold: Keep the neck long, head down.
Rock gently side to side if pleasant.
exit: Release the arms and extend the legs one at a time.

wind-release-pose.breath: Exhale to draw the knees in, inhale to ease slightly.

chaise.name: Chair
chaise.summary: A squat-like bend of the knees with arms raised that strongly builds the legs and back.

entry: From Mountain, feet together or hip-width apart.
Bend the knees and send the hips back.
Raise the arms in line with the torso.
hold: Weight in the heels, knees behind the toes.
Lengthen the back without arching.
Shoulders away from the ears.
exit: Straighten the legs and return to Mountain.

chaise.breath: Breathe steadily; do not hold the breath.

grand-ecart-facial-debout.name: Wide-Legged Forward Fold
grand-ecart-facial-debout.summary: A forward bend with legs wide apart that stretches the inner and back legs.
contraindications: Low back pain: keep the back flat

entry: Step the feet wide, parallel.
Hands on hips, lengthen the torso.
Hinge forward from the hips.
hold: Hands on the floor under shoulders or on blocks.
Let the head lower if comfortable.
Keep the legs active.
exit: Hands to hips, rise with a long back, then step the feet in.

grand-ecart-facial-debout.breath: Exhale to fold, inhale to lengthen.

supine-spinal-twist-pose-ii.name: Supine Spinal Twist
supine-spinal-twist-pose-ii.summary: A gentle twist lying on the back with knees dropped to one side that relaxes the spine and low back.

entry: Lie on the back and bend the knees.
Open the arms into a T.
Let the knees fall to one side.
hold: Keep both shoulders down if possible.
Turn the head the other way if comfortable.
Support the knees with a cushion if needed.
exit: Bring the knees back to center, then switch sides.

supine-spinal-twist-pose-ii.breath: Breathe deeply into the belly and ribs.

planche.name: Plank
planche.summary: A hold on hands and toes with the body in one line that strengthens the core and upper body.
contraindications: Low back pain: lower the knees

entry: From tabletop, step the feet back one at a time.
Hands under shoulders, fingers spread.
Line up head, hips and heels.
hold: Engage the belly; don't let the hips sag.
Press the floor away, shoulder blades wide.
Reach the heels back.
exit: Lower the knees or move to Downward Dog.

cobra.name: Cobra
cobra.summary: A prone backbend that opens the chest and strengthens the back muscles.

entry: Lie on the belly, hands under shoulders.
Elbows close to the body, tops of feet down.
Press lightly to lift the chest.
hold: Keep the pelvis down and shoulders low.
Neck in line with the spine.
Use mainly the back muscles.
exit: Exhale and lower the chest and forehead gently.

cobra.breath: Inhale to rise, exhale to lower.

cat-cow-pose.name: Cat-Cow
cat-cow-pose.summary: A hands-and-knees flow between rounding and arching the back, linked to the breath, to mobilize the spine.
contraindications: Neck injury: keep the head neutral

entry: Come to tabletop, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Start from a neutral spine.
hold: Inhale: drop the belly, chest forward, gaze slightly up.
Exhale: round the back, chin toward chest.
Repeat slowly for several rounds.
exit: Return to a neutral back or sit back into Child's Pose.

cat-cow-pose.breath: Inhale into Cow, exhale into Cat.

guerrier-2.name: Warrior II
guerrier-2.summary: A wide-legged standing pose with the front knee bent and arms extended that strengthens the legs and opens the hips.

entry: Step the feet wide apart.
Front foot forward, back foot slightly turned in.
Bend the front knee over the ankle.
hold: Arms parallel to the floor, shoulders relaxed.
Torso upright over the pelvis.
Gaze over the front hand.
exit: Straighten the front leg, step the feet in, switch sides.

guerrier-2.breath: Long, steady breathing throughout the hold.

pont.name: Bridge
pont.summary: A supine backbend lifting the hips that strengthens glutes and back and opens the chest.
contraindications: Neck injury: don't turn the head

entry: Lie on the back, knees bent, feet flat hip-width apart.
Arms by the sides, palms down.
Press through the feet to lift the hips.
hold: Knees parallel over the ankles.
Gently draw the shoulder blades under.
Keep the neck free, gaze up.
exit: Roll the spine down one vertebra at a time.

pont.breath: Inhale to lift, breathe into the chest, exhale to lower.

neck-twists-close-up.name: Neck Rotations
neck-twists-close-up.summary: A gentle neck mobilization slowly turning the head side to side, often seated, to release neck tension.
contraindications: Cervical disc issues: seek medical advice

entry: Sit or stand with a long spine.
Shoulders relaxed, chin level.
hold: Slowly turn the head to one side without forcing.
Return to center, then turn to the other side.
Repeat a few times at your own pace.
exit: Bring the head to center and pause for a few breaths.

neck-twists-close-up.breath: Exhale to turn, inhale back to center.

sun-salutation.name: Sun Salutation
sun-salutation.summary: A dynamic sequence of breath-linked poses (Mountain, Forward Fold, lunge or Plank, Cobra, Dog…) that warms the whole body.
contraindications: Back, wrist or shoulder injury: modify

entry: Begin in Mountain, palms together at the chest.
Inhale arms up, exhale into Forward Fold.
hold: Flow through lunge or Plank, lower down, Cobra, then Downward Dog.
Return to Forward Fold and rise with arms up.
Match each movement to an inhale or exhale.
exit: Finish in Mountain, palms at the chest.

sun-salutation.breath: One movement per inhale or exhale.

bateau.name: Boat
bateau.summary: A seated balance on the sit bones with legs and torso lifted in a V that strongly works the core.
contraindications: Low back pain: keep knees bent

entry: Sit with knees bent, feet on the floor.
Lean back slightly with a long spine.
Lift the feet, shins parallel to the floor.
hold: Reach the arms forward.
Straighten the legs if possible without rounding.
Keep the chest open.
exit: Lower the feet and release.

bateau.breath: Breathe steadily; do not hold the breath.

papillon.name: Bound Angle
papillon.summary: A seated pose with soles together and knees open that releases the hips and groin.
contraindications: Knee or groin injury: support the knees

entry: Sit, bend the knees and join the soles of the feet.
Let the knees open to the sides.
Hold feet or ankles; raise the hips if needed.
hold: Lengthen the spine.
Let the knees lower without pushing.
Optionally fold forward with a long back.
exit: Bring the knees together with the hands and extend the legs.

papillon.breath: Slow breathing; let the exhale soften the hips.

triangle.name: Triangle
triangle.summary: A standing pose with straight legs wide apart and torso tilted sideways that stretches the sides, legs and chest.

entry: Step the feet wide, front foot turned forward.
Arms parallel to the floor.
Reach the torso forward, then tilt it sideways.
hold: Lower hand on shin, block or floor.
Top arm toward the ceiling, chest open.
Keep both sides of the waist long.
exit: Press into the feet to rise, then switch sides.

triangle.breath: Breathe broadly into the ribs, steadily.

baton.name: Staff
baton.summary: A seated pose with legs extended forward and an upright back, the base for seated poses.
benefits: Stretches the back of the legs
contraindications: Low back pain: raise the hips
Tight hamstrings: bend the knees slightly

entry: Sit with legs extended, feet flexed.
Hands on the floor beside the hips.
Sit evenly on the sit bones.
hold: Lengthen the spine, shoulders relaxed.
Active thighs, heels reaching forward.
Chin slightly tucked.
exit: Release the legs and move on.

baton.breath: Calm breathing, growing taller on each inhale.

guerrier-1.name: Warrior I
guerrier-1.summary: A standing lunge with the back foot down, hips facing forward and arms raised, building the legs and opening the front body.
contraindications: High blood pressure: hands on hips

entry: From Mountain, take a big step back.
Back foot flat, turned out.
Bend the front knee over the ankle.
hold: Square the hips toward the front.
Raise the arms, shoulders relaxed.
Ground the back heel.
exit: Hands down or step the back foot in, then switch sides.

guerrier-1.breath: Inhale to raise the arms; keep the breath steady.

deesse.name: Goddess
deesse.summary: A wide-legged squat with toes turned out and knees bent that builds the legs and opens the hips.
contraindications: Low back pain: keep pelvis neutral

entry: Step the feet wide, toes turned out.
Bend the knees in line with the toes.
Lower the hips, torso upright.
hold: Arms in cactus or hands at the chest.
Knees pressing outward.
Tailbone toward the floor.
exit: Straighten the legs and step the feet in.

deesse.breath: Full breathing; exhale to ground down.

chair-mountain-pose.name: Chair Mountain
chair-mountain-pose.summary: A seated version of Mountain on a chair to work on alignment and presence accessibly.
contraindications: Use a stable chair without wheels

entry: Sit near the front edge of a stable chair.
Feet flat, knees over the ankles.
Lengthen the spine, crown rising.
hold: Hands on the thighs, shoulders relaxed.
Lightly engage the belly.
Steady gaze forward.
exit: Release and lean back on the chair if needed.

planche-laterale.name: Side Plank
planche-laterale.summary: A balance on one hand and the edges of the feet, body sideways, that strengthens arms, shoulders and sides.

entry: From Plank, roll onto the outer edge of one foot.
Supporting hand under the shoulder.
Stack the feet or lower the bottom knee.
hold: Lift the hips, body in one line.
Top arm toward the ceiling.
Press actively through the supporting hand.
exit: Return to Plank, then switch sides.

guirlande.name: Garland (Yogi Squat)
guirlande.summary: A deep squat with feet apart and palms together that opens the hips and stretches the low back.

entry: Feet slightly wider than hips, toes turned out.
Bend the knees and lower the hips.
Use a block under hips or heels if needed.
hold: Palms together at the chest, elbows against knees.
Lengthen the spine.
Heels grounded.
exit: Hands down and straighten the legs, or sit down.

guirlande.breath: Slow breathing, lengthening the back on the inhale.

half-pigeon-pose.name: Half Pigeon
half-pigeon-pose.summary: A floor hip opener with one leg bent in front and the other extended behind, stretching glutes and hip flexors.
contraindications: Knee injury: try Thread the Needle

entry: From Dog or tabletop, bring one knee behind the wrist.
Extend the back leg, top of foot down.
Support the front hip with a cushion if it lifts.
hold: Hips level, facing forward.
Stay upright or fold the torso forward.
Flex the front foot to protect the knee.
exit: Hands down, step back to Dog, then switch sides.

half-pigeon-pose.breath: Slow breathing; soften the hip on each exhale.

pince-assise.name: Seated Forward Bend
pince-assise.summary: A seated forward fold with legs extended that stretches the whole back body and quiets the mind.

entry: From Staff, lengthen the spine.
Hinge forward from the hips.
Bend the knees or use a strap if needed.
hold: Hands on legs, ankles or feet.
Relax neck and shoulders.
Lead with the belly, not the head.
exit: Inhale and rise with a long back.

pince-assise.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to fold gently deeper.

demi-seigneur-poissons.name: Half Lord of the Fishes
demi-seigneur-poissons.summary: A seated twist with one leg crossed over the other that mobilizes the spine and opens the shoulders.
contraindications: Herniated disc or acute back pain

entry: Sit, bend one leg and place the foot outside the opposite knee.
Keep the other leg extended or folded.
Lengthen the spine.
hold: Turn toward the lifted knee, back hand on the floor.
Opposite arm hugs the knee or elbow outside it.
Keep the sit bones grounded.
exit: Slowly turn back to center, then switch sides.

demi-seigneur-poissons.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to twist a little further.

angle-lateral.name: Extended Side Angle
angle-lateral.summary: A side lunge with forearm or hand near the front foot and the top arm reaching overhead, stretching the whole side body.

entry: From Warrior II, bend the front knee over the ankle.
Forearm on the thigh, or hand on floor or block.
Reach the top arm over the ear.
hold: One line from back heel to fingertips.
Open the chest upward.
Outer edge of the back foot grounded.
exit: Rise back to Warrior II, then switch sides.

angle-lateral.breath: Breathe into the stretched side, evenly.

seated-straddle-pose.name: Seated Wide-Angle Forward Bend
seated-straddle-pose.summary: A seated pose with legs spread wide, often folding forward, that stretches adductors and hamstrings.
contraindications: Low back pain: raise the hips

entry: From Staff, spread the legs wide.
Kneecaps and toes pointing up.
Raise the hips if the back rounds.
hold: Lengthen the back, hands in front.
Walk the hands forward only while the back stays long.
Keep the legs active.
exit: Rise and bring the legs together with the hands.

seated-straddle-pose.breath: Exhale to fold, inhale to lengthen.

guerrier-3.name: Warrior III
guerrier-3.summary: A one-legged balance with torso and back leg parallel to the floor that strengthens the standing leg and back.
contraindications: Balance issues: hands on wall or blocks

entry: From High Lunge or Mountain, shift weight onto one leg.
Tip the torso forward as the back leg lifts.
Hands on hips, on blocks, or arms forward.
hold: Hips level, back toes pointing down.
One line from head to heel.
Standing leg active, knee soft.
exit: Lower the back foot, return to standing, switch sides.

guerrier-3.breath: Calm, steady breathing to support balance.

diamant.name: Thunderbolt (Vajrasana)
diamant.summary: A kneeling seat on the heels with an upright back, used for breathing and meditation.
contraindications: Cushion between hips and heels if needed

entry: Kneel with knees together.
Sit back on the heels, big toes close.
Add a cushion if knees or ankles strain.
hold: Hands on the thighs, spine long.
Shoulders relaxed, chin slightly tucked.
exit: Lean forward, hands down, and release the legs.

guerrier-inverse.name: Reverse Warrior
guerrier-inverse.summary: A Warrior II variation where the torso leans back with the arm raised to stretch the side body.

entry: Start in Warrior II.
Turn the front palm up.
Raise the front arm and lean the torso back.
hold: Back hand slides along the back leg, lightly.
Front knee stays bent over the ankle.
Keep both sides long.
exit: Return to Warrior II, then switch sides.

guerrier-inverse.breath: Inhale to open the side; breathe smoothly.

bebe-heureux.name: Happy Baby
bebe-heureux.summary: A supine pose with knees drawn toward the armpits and feet held that opens the hips and releases the low back.
contraindications: Neck pain: cushion under the head

entry: Lie on the back and draw the knees to the chest.
Open the knees toward the armpits.
Hold the outer feet, ankles or shins.
hold: Soles toward the ceiling, ankles over knees.
Let the sacrum settle down.
Rock gently if pleasant.
exit: Release the feet and lower the legs.

arbre.name: Tree
arbre.summary: A one-legged standing balance with the other sole against the standing leg that builds stability and focus.
contraindications: Avoid placing the foot on the knee

entry: From Mountain, shift weight onto one leg.
Place the other sole on ankle, calf or inner thigh.
Open the bent knee to the side.
hold: Hands at the chest or arms overhead.
Press foot and leg into each other.
Fix the gaze on one point.
exit: Lower the foot, return to Mountain, switch sides.

relaxation-ventre.name: Reverse Corpse
relaxation-ventre.summary: A prone relaxation, head turned or resting on the arms, used between belly-down poses or at the end of class.
contraindications: Breathing discomfort: lie on the back

entry: Lie on the belly, legs slightly apart.
Arms by the sides or forehead on stacked hands.
hold: Relax hips, shoulders and jaw.
Switch the head side halfway if turned.
exit: Hands under shoulders, press back to Child's Pose or tabletop.

relaxation-ventre.breath: Feel the belly press into the floor on each inhale.

resp-alternee.name: Alternate Nostril Breathing (Nadi Shodhana)
resp-alternee.summary: A seated pranayama alternating inhales and exhales through each nostril to balance and calm.
contraindications: Never force or hold the breath unguided

entry: Sit comfortably with an upright spine.
Right hand near the nose, index and middle fingers folded or on the brow.
Gently close the right nostril with the thumb.
hold: Inhale left, close left, exhale right.
Inhale right, close right, exhale left.
Continue several rounds without strain.
exit: Finish with an exhale through the left, release the hand and breathe naturally.

resp-alternee.breath: Slow, quiet, even breathing without strain.

tete-au-genou.name: Head-to-Knee Forward Bend
tete-au-genou.summary: A seated forward bend over one straight leg with the other bent, stretching hamstrings and back asymmetrically.
contraindications: Knee injury: support the bent knee

entry: From Staff, bend one knee and place the foot by the opposite inner thigh.
Turn the torso slightly toward the straight leg.
Lengthen the spine.
hold: Hinge from the hips over the straight leg.
Hands on leg, foot or strap.
Neck relaxed, back as long as possible.
exit: Rise with a long back, extend the leg, switch sides.

tete-au-genou.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to fold.

pyramide.name: Pyramid
pyramide.summary: A standing forward bend in a short straight-legged stance that intensely stretches the back of the front leg.
contraindications: Back pain: flat back, hands on blocks

entry: From Mountain, step one foot back a short distance, hip-width apart.
Hips square, legs straight but not locked.
Lengthen the torso, then hinge from the hips.
hold: Hands on floor, blocks, or behind the back.
Long back, relaxed neck.
Weight spread between both feet.
exit: Rise with a long back, step in, switch sides.

pyramide.breath: Exhale to fold, inhale to lengthen.

chameau.name: Camel
chameau.summary: A kneeling backbend reaching for the heels or the low back that broadly opens the chest and front body.

entry: Kneel with knees hip-width, thighs vertical.
Hands on the lower back.
Lift the chest and begin to lean back.
hold: Hands on heels or stay on the back.
Hips over the knees.
Support the neck; don't drop the head if uncomfortable.
exit: Hands to back, rise leading with the chest, then rest in Child's Pose.

chameau.breath: Breathe into the open chest without holding.

seated-neck-rolls.name: Seated Neck Rolls
seated-neck-rolls.summary: Slow circular head movements while seated to loosen the neck and shoulders.
contraindications: Neck injury or arthritis: front half-circles only
Cervical disc issues: seek medical advice

entry: Sit upright, shoulders relaxed.
Let the chin drop toward the chest.
hold: Slowly roll the head toward one shoulder, then the other.
Limit tilting back if uncomfortable.
Change direction after a few rounds.
exit: Bring the head to center and pause for a few breaths.

seated-neck-rolls.breath: Slow, smooth breathing matched to the movement.

flamingo-pose.name: Flamingo
flamingo-pose.summary: A one-legged standing balance with the other knee lifted or leg extended forward that builds the standing leg and focus.

entry: From Mountain, shift weight onto one leg.
Lift the other knee to hip height.
Hold the knee or extend the leg forward if possible.
hold: Hips level, torso upright.
Standing leg active, knee soft.
Fix the gaze on one point.
exit: Lower the foot, return to Mountain, switch sides.

reverse-pigeon-pose.name: Reclined Pigeon (Figure Four)
reverse-pigeon-pose.summary: A supine hip opener with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee that gently stretches glutes and piriformis.
contraindications: Knee injury: flex the foot, don't force

entry: Lie on the back, knees bent, feet down.
Cross the right ankle over the left thigh, foot flexed.
Thread the hand through and hold behind the left thigh.
hold: Draw the legs gently toward the chest.
Keep head and shoulders down.
Let the crossed knee open without forcing.
exit: Release, place the feet down and switch sides.

reverse-pigeon-pose.breath: Slow breathing; soften the hip on the exhale.

fil-aiguille.name: Thread the Needle
fil-aiguille.summary: A twist from tabletop with one arm slid under the body, shoulder and temple down, stretching the shoulders and upper back.

entry: Start in tabletop.
Slide one arm under the body, palm up.
Rest the shoulder and temple on the floor.
hold: Hips over the knees.
Other hand on the floor or arm reaching forward.
Relax the neck.
exit: Press through the floor hand back to tabletop, then switch sides.

fil-aiguille.breath: Breathe slowly into the upper back.

papillon-allonge.name: Reclining Bound Angle
papillon-allonge.summary: A supine relaxing pose with soles together and knees open that opens the hips and chest.
contraindications: Groin or knee injury: support the knees
Low back pain: cushion under pelvis or back

entry: From seated Bound Angle, lie back on the floor or a bolster.
Let the knees open, supported by blocks if needed.
Arms by the sides, palms up.
hold: Relax hips, belly and shoulders.
Stay several minutes with eyes closed.
exit: Bring the knees together with the hands, roll to one side and sit up.

papillon-allonge.breath: Slow breathing into belly and chest.

sauterelle.name: Locust
sauterelle.summary: A prone backbend lifting chest and legs that strengthens the whole back body.
contraindications: Acute low back or neck injury

entry: Lie on the belly, arms by the sides, forehead down.
Legs together or hip-width.
Engage the legs and lengthen from the pelvis.
hold: Lift chest, arms and legs.
Neck long, gaze down ahead.
Pubic bone grounded.
exit: Exhale to lower, then rest with the head turned.

sauterelle.breath: Inhale to lift; keep breathing steadily.

sphinx.name: Sphinx
sphinx.summary: A gentle prone backbend on the forearms that opens the chest without overloading the back.

entry: Lie on the belly, legs hip-width.
Elbows under shoulders, forearms parallel.
Lift the chest, drawing gently forward.
hold: Shoulders away from the ears.
Pelvis down, glutes soft.
Neck long.
exit: Lower the chest and forehead and rest.

sphinx.breath: Calm breathing into the open chest.

chiot.name: Puppy
chiot.summary: Halfway between Child's Pose and Dog: hips over knees, arms extended and chest toward the floor to stretch the shoulders and back.
contraindications: Neck pain: forehead on a block

entry: Start in tabletop.
Walk the hands forward a few steps.
Lower the chest toward the floor, hips over knees.
hold: Forehead on the floor or a prop.
Arms active, elbows lifted.
Lengthen from hips to hands.
exit: Walk the hands back to tabletop or sit into Child's Pose.

chiot.breath: Breathe slowly into the back and chest.

demi-lune.name: Half Moon
demi-lune.summary: A balance on one leg and one hand, body open to the side with the top leg lifted, that strengthens and stretches at once.

entry: From Triangle, bend the front knee and place the hand ahead of the foot on floor or block.
Shift weight onto the front leg.
Lift the back leg to hip height.
hold: Open hips and chest to the side.
Top arm toward the ceiling.
Lifted foot active and flexed.
exit: Bend the standing leg, lower the back foot, return to Triangle or a lunge.

demi-lune.breath: Calm breathing to steady the balance.

porte.name: Gate
porte.summary: A kneeling side stretch with one leg extended to the side that opens the whole side body.
contraindications: Knee injury: blanket under the knee

entry: Kneel and extend one leg to the side, foot down.
Line the foot up with the standing knee.
Raise the arm opposite the extended leg.
hold: Lean toward the extended leg, hand resting on it.
Top arm over the ear.
Chest open; don't collapse forward.
exit: Rise, bring the leg in, then switch sides.

porte.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to side-bend.

reclined-big-toe-pose-straps.name: Reclining Hand-to-Big-Toe (with strap)
reclined-big-toe-pose-straps.summary: A supine stretch with one leg lifted and held by a strap that stretches the back of the leg without loading the back.

entry: Lie on the back with knees bent.
Loop the strap around the sole of one foot.
Extend the leg upward, holding the strap.
hold: Other leg straight on the floor or bent with foot down.
Shoulders and head relaxed on the floor.
Draw the leg closer without lifting the hips.
exit: Bend the knee, remove the strap and switch sides.

reclined-big-toe-pose-straps.breath: Slow breathing; soften the back of the leg on the exhale.

shoulder-socket-rotation.name: Shoulder Rotations
shoulder-socket-rotation.summary: A joint warm-up: fingertips on the shoulders, drawing large circles with the elbows.
contraindications: Shoulder injury or dislocation: small circles

entry: Sit or stand with an upright spine.
Place the fingertips on the shoulders.
hold: Slowly draw large circles with the elbows.
Do a few rounds, then reverse direction.
exit: Release the arms and notice the shoulders.

shoulder-socket-rotation.breath: Inhale as the elbows rise, exhale as they lower.

charrue.name: Plow
charrue.summary: A supine inversion where the legs pass overhead toward the floor, strongly stretching the back and neck.
benefits: Stretches the back of the legs

entry: Lie on the back, arms by the sides, blanket under shoulders if needed.
Lift legs and hips, hands supporting the back.
Lower the feet behind the head to the floor or a prop.
hold: Keep the neck free, gaze toward the belly.
Arms on the floor or hands on the back.
Keep holds short at first.
exit: Hands down, slowly roll the spine down to the hips.

charrue.breath: Calm breathing; ease off if the breath feels restricted.

revolved-eight-point-crescent-moon-pose.name: Revolved Crescent Lunge
revolved-eight-point-crescent-moon-pose.summary: A high lunge with a torso twist, elbow or hand outside the front knee, combining leg strength with spinal rotation.

entry: From a high or low lunge, palms together at the chest.
Rotate the torso toward the front leg.
Hook the elbow or hand outside the front knee.
hold: Lengthen the spine before twisting further.
Front knee over the ankle.
Lower the back knee if needed.
exit: Unwind to center, hands down and switch sides.

revolved-eight-point-crescent-moon-pose.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to twist.

chat-vache-assis.name: Seated Cat-Cow
chat-vache-assis.summary: A seated version of Cat-Cow, hands on knees, alternating a rounded back and open chest with the breath.
benefits: Accessible on a chair or floor

entry: Sit cross-legged or on a chair, hands on knees.
Spine long, shoulders relaxed.
hold: Inhale: open the chest, gently arch the back.
Exhale: round the back, chin toward chest.
Repeat slowly for several rounds.
exit: Return to a neutral spine and breathe for a moment.

chat-vache-assis.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to round.

chaturanga.name: Four-Limbed Staff (Chaturanga)
chaturanga.summary: A low plank with elbows bent close to the body that strongly builds arms, shoulders and core.

entry: Start in Plank, shoulders over wrists.
Shift weight slightly forward.
Bend the elbows straight back, close to the ribs.
hold: Lower until shoulders are level with elbows, no lower.
Body in one line, belly engaged.
Keep the shoulders from dropping.
exit: Lower to the floor or move into Cobra or Upward Dog.

side-lying-corpse-pose.name: Side-Lying Savasana
side-lying-corpse-pose.summary: A Savasana variation lying on the side with props, ideal in pregnancy or when lying on the back is uncomfortable.
contraindications: Shoulder pain: switch sides or add a cushion

entry: Lie on the side, preferably the left in pregnancy.
Cushion under the head and between the knees.
Bend the knees slightly.
hold: Relax the whole body.
Stay several minutes with eyes closed.
exit: Press up with the hands to sit slowly.

bharadvaja.name: Bharadvaja's Twist
bharadvaja.summary: A gentle seated twist with both legs folded to one side that mobilizes the spine and opens the shoulders.
contraindications: Herniated disc or acute back pain
Knee injury: sit on a blanket

entry: Sit and fold both legs to the left side.
Raise the right hip on a blanket if needed.
Lengthen the spine.
hold: Turn the torso to the right.
Left hand on the right knee, right hand on the floor behind.
Keep the sit bones heavy.
exit: Slowly return to center, then switch sides.

bharadvaja.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to twist.

tete-vache.name: Cow Face
tete-vache.summary: A seated pose with stacked knees and hands clasping behind the back that opens the hips and shoulders.
contraindications: Knee injury: extend the bottom leg

entry: Sit and cross the legs, stacking the knees.
Feet beside the hips; sit on a cushion if needed.
Raise one arm, bend the elbow, hand down the back; other hand reaches up from below.
hold: Clasp the hands or hold a strap.
Long back, top elbow pointing up.
Sit bones grounded.
exit: Release the arms, uncross the legs, switch sides.

tete-vache.breath: Calm breathing, opening the chest on the inhale.

main-gros-orteil.name: Standing Hand-to-Big-Toe
main-gros-orteil.summary: A standing balance holding the big toe with the lifted leg extended forward or to the side, combining strength, flexibility and balance.
contraindications: Tight hamstrings: bent knee or strap

entry: From Mountain, shift weight onto one leg.
Lift the other knee and hold the big toe or use a strap.
Extend the leg forward if possible.
hold: Long back, shoulders over hips.
Standing leg active.
Option: open the leg to the side.
exit: Bring the leg to center, bend the knee and lower the foot.

main-gros-orteil.breath: Calm breathing to steady the balance.

cycling-pose.name: Leg Cycling
cycling-pose.summary: A supine exercise mimicking pedaling a bicycle with the legs to strengthen the abs and mobilize the hips.

entry: Lie on the back, arms by the sides, palms down.
Lift the legs with knees bent.
hold: Slowly pedal forward as on a bicycle.
Keep the low back in contact with the floor.
Reverse direction after a few rounds.
exit: Lower the feet and release.

danseur.name: Dancer
danseur.summary: A standing balance holding the back foot, torso tipping forward and leg pressing up, combining balance and backbend.

entry: From Mountain, bend one knee and hold the foot or ankle from the inside.
Raise the other arm forward.
Start with the knees close.
hold: Press the foot into the hand and tip the torso forward.
Standing leg active, hips level.
Steady gaze ahead.
exit: Rise, release the foot and switch sides.

grand-ecart.name: Splits (Hanumanasana)
grand-ecart.summary: An advanced pose with one leg extended forward and the other back on the floor, deeply stretching hamstrings and hip flexors.
contraindications: Never force: blocks under hands and hips

entry: From Low Lunge, shift the hips back and straighten the front leg.
Gradually slide the front heel forward.
Support the hips with a block or bolster.
hold: Hips facing forward.
Hands on blocks on each side.
Stay where the breath stays calm.
exit: Bend the front knee, return to Low Lunge, switch sides.

grand-ecart.breath: Slow breathing; never force on the exhale.

poisson.name: Fish
poisson.summary: A supine backbend lifting the chest on the forearms that opens the throat and rib cage.

entry: Lie on the back, legs straight or bent.
Slide the hands under the hips, elbows close.
Press into the forearms to lift the chest.
hold: Let the crown lightly touch the floor, no weight on the head.
Option: block or bolster under the back.
Chest open toward the ceiling.
exit: Lift the head slightly, tuck the chin and lower the back.

poisson.breath: Breathe deeply into the open chest.

arc.name: Bow
arc.summary: A prone backbend holding the ankles, body shaped like a bow, that strongly opens the front body.

entry: Lie on the belly and bend the knees.
Hold the outer ankles.
Knees hip-width apart.
hold: Press the feet into the hands to lift chest and thighs.
Shoulders open, neck long.
Keep the breath flowing.
exit: Exhale, release the ankles and rest on the belly.

arc.breath: Inhale to lift; do not hold the breath.

shoulderstand-pose.name: Shoulderstand
shoulderstand-pose.summary: An inversion on the shoulders with legs vertical and back supported by the hands, to be practiced with care and preparation.
contraindications: High blood pressure, glaucoma, heart conditions

entry: Lie down, shoulders on a folded blanket, head on the floor.
Lift legs and hips, hands supporting the back.
Gradually stack legs and hips over the shoulders.
hold: Elbows close, weight on the shoulders, not the neck.
Legs active toward the ceiling.
Start with short holds.
exit: Bend the knees and slowly roll the spine down.

shoulderstand-pose.breath: Calm breathing; come down if the breath gets restricted.

fente-laterale.name: Side Lunge (Skandasana)
fente-laterale.summary: A wide side squat with one leg bent and the other straight that stretches adductors and hamstrings and strengthens the legs.
contraindications: Stiff ankles: block under heel or hands down

entry: Step the feet wide, toes slightly out.
Bend one knee and shift the hips to that side.
Straighten the other leg, toes up.
hold: Hands on the floor or together at the chest.
Heel of the bent leg down if possible.
Long back.
exit: Press through the feet back to center, then switch sides.

fente-laterale.breath: Slow breathing; soften the inner thigh on the exhale.

aigle.name: Eagle
aigle.summary: A standing balance with legs and arms wrapped and knees bent that stretches the upper back and sharpens focus.
contraindications: Shoulder injury: simply cross the arms
Balance issues: toes on the floor

entry: From Chair, cross one thigh over the other.
Hook the foot behind the calf or rest the toes down.
Cross the arms, elbow on the standing-leg side below.
hold: Palms together or backs of hands touching.
Lift the elbows, shoulders low.
Sink the hips, steady gaze.
exit: Unwind arms and legs, return to Mountain, switch sides.

aigle.breath: Breathe steadily into the upper back.

lezard.name: Lizard
lezard.summary: A deep low lunge with both hands inside the front foot. It strongly opens the hips, groin and hip flexors.

entry: From Downward-Facing Dog, step the right foot outside the right hand.
Lower the back knee if needed.
Place both hands inside the front foot.
hold: Let the pelvis sink toward the floor.
Option: lower to forearms or a block.
exit: Press back up onto the hands and step back to Down Dog.
Repeat on the other side.

lezard.breath: Breathe slowly into the hips, softening a little more with each exhale.

planche-inversee.name: Upward Plank
planche-inversee.summary: A face-up position where the body forms a straight line supported by hands and feet. It strengthens the back body and opens the front.
contraindications: Neck issues: keep the chin tucked

entry: Sit with legs straight, hands behind the hips, fingers toward the feet.
Press hands and feet to lift the hips.
Line up shoulders, hips and ankles.
hold: Push the floor away and lift the chest.
Keep the neck long or let the head release gently.
exit: Lower the hips to the floor with control.

planche-inversee.breath: Inhale to lift, then breathe steadily with an open chest.

heros.name: Hero
heros.summary: A kneeling seated pose with the hips between the heels. It stretches the thighs and ankles and supports an upright seat for meditation.
contraindications: Knee discomfort: sit on a block

entry: Kneel with knees together, feet slightly wider than hips.
Roll the calf muscles outward with the hands.
Sit between the heels, on a block if needed.
hold: Lengthen the spine, hands resting on the thighs.
Keep feet straight, toes pointing back.
exit: Lean forward onto the hands and extend the legs back one at a time.

heros.breath: Breathe calmly and evenly with a long spine.

chien-tete-en-haut.name: Upward-Facing Dog
chien-tete-en-haut.summary: A backbend on straight arms with legs and hips lifted off the floor. It opens the chest and strengthens arms and back.

entry: Lie on the belly, hands under the shoulders, tops of the feet down.
Press into the hands and straighten the arms.
Lift thighs and hips off the floor.
hold: Draw shoulders away from the ears, chest forward.
Keep legs active and neck long.
exit: Lift the hips back to Down Dog or lower to the floor.

chien-tete-en-haut.breath: Inhale to open the chest, exhale to leave the pose.

guerrier-humble.name: Humble Warrior
guerrier-humble.summary: A warrior lunge with hands clasped behind the back and the torso bowing inside the front knee. It opens shoulders and hips with a sense of surrender.

entry: From Warrior I, interlace the fingers behind the back.
Inhale to lift the chest.
Exhale and bow the torso inside the front knee.
hold: Let the arms float away from the back.
Keep the back leg strong and the head heavy.
exit: Inhale to rise, then release the hands.

guerrier-humble.breath: Exhale to bow, then breathe slowly in the fold.

flexion-arriere-debout.name: Standing Backbend
flexion-arriere-debout.summary: A gentle backbend while standing, arms overhead or hands on the lower back. It opens the front body and wakes up the spine.

entry: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Hands on the lower back or arms overhead.
Inhale to lengthen, then lift the chest up and back.
hold: Keep hips over feet and glutes moderate.
Keep the neck long, without crunching it.
exit: Return upright, leading with the chest.

flexion-arriere-debout.breath: Inhale to open and keep the breath flowing.

dauphin.name: Dolphin
dauphin.summary: A forearm version of Downward-Facing Dog. It builds shoulder and upper-back strength and prepares for inversions.

entry: From all fours, lower the forearms, elbows under shoulders.
Tuck the toes and lift the hips.
Walk the feet slightly toward the elbows.
hold: Press the forearms down and lift shoulders away from the ears.
Bend the knees if the back rounds.
exit: Lower the knees and rest in Child's Pose.

dauphin.breath: Breathe fully and steadily without holding.

jambes-au-mur.name: Legs Up the Wall
jambes-au-mur.summary: A restorative pose lying on the back with legs resting vertically against a wall. It calms the nervous system and relieves the legs.

entry: Sit sideways with one hip against the wall.
Swing the legs up the wall as you lie back.
Move the hips closer to the wall as flexibility allows.
hold: Relax the arms and close the eyes.
Stay several minutes, a cushion under the pelvis if desired.
exit: Bend the knees, roll to one side and sit up slowly.

jambes-au-mur.breath: Let the breath become slow and natural.

poirier.name: Headstand
poirier.summary: An inversion balanced on the forearms and crown of the head, fingers interlaced. It builds core strength, balance and focus.

entry: Kneel, forearms down, fingers interlaced, elbows shoulder-width.
Place the crown of the head against the hands.
Lift the hips and walk the feet toward the face.
Lift one leg, then the other, with control.
hold: Press through the forearms to keep weight off the neck.
Body aligned, legs active.
exit: Lower one leg at a time and rest in Child's Pose.

poirier.breath: Breathe slowly; come down if the breath strains.

lotus-mudra.name: Lotus Mudra
lotus-mudra.summary: A hand gesture shaped like an open flower in front of the heart, thumbs and little fingers touching. It symbolizes openness and invites softness.

entry: Sit comfortably with a tall spine.
Bring the palms together in front of the heart.
Keep thumbs and little fingers touching and open the other fingers like petals.
hold: Hold for a few breaths with relaxed shoulders.
exit: Close the hands to prayer and rest them on the thighs.

lotus-mudra.breath: Breathe softly and deeply, attention at the center of the chest.

lotus.name: Lotus
lotus.summary: A cross-legged seat with each foot resting on the opposite thigh. A stable meditation seat that requires deep hip opening.

entry: Sit with legs straight; bend the right knee and place the foot high on the left thigh.
Bend the left knee and place the foot on the right thigh.
Knees toward the floor, spine tall.
hold: Hands on the knees, shoulders relaxed.
Alternate the cross from one practice to the next.
exit: Uncross slowly with the hands and extend the legs.

lotus.breath: Breathe naturally and quietly, gaze inward.

roue.name: Wheel
roue.summary: A full backbend on hands and feet, the body forming an arch. It strongly opens chest and shoulders and strengthens arms and legs.
contraindications: High blood pressure or heart condition

entry: Lie on the back with feet near the hips.
Place hands by the ears, fingers toward the shoulders.
Lift the hips, rest on the crown, then straighten the arms.
hold: Press through hands and feet, knees parallel.
Let the head hang freely.
exit: Tuck the chin and lower the back slowly to the floor.
Rest with knees bent or hugged in.

roue.breath: Breathe into the open chest without holding the breath.

corbeau.name: Crow
corbeau.summary: An arm balance with the knees resting on the back of bent arms. It builds arm strength, core engagement and focus.

entry: Squat with hands shoulder-width on the floor, fingers spread.
Bend the elbows and place the knees on the backs of the arms.
Shift forward and lift one foot, then the other.
hold: Gaze slightly ahead, core engaged.
Draw the heels toward the hips.
exit: Lower the feet and sit back or fold forward.

corbeau.breath: Keep the breath steady despite the effort.

easy-side-reclining-leg-lift-pose.name: Easy Side-Lying Leg Lift
easy-side-reclining-leg-lift-pose.summary: Lying on the side with the head supported, you lift the top leg. It strengthens the abductors and builds lateral stability.

entry: Lie on the right side, head resting on the arm or hand.
Stack shoulders, hips and feet.
Lift the left leg without rolling the pelvis.
hold: Keep the foot flexed and the torso steady.
Option: bend the knee or pulse the leg.
exit: Lower the leg and switch sides.

easy-side-reclining-leg-lift-pose.breath: Exhale to lift the leg, inhale to lower it.

grue.name: Crane
grue.summary: An arm balance similar to Crow, but with straight arms and knees high on the arms. It demands more strength and core control.

entry: Squat with hands shoulder-width on the floor.
Place the knees high on the backs of the arms, near the armpits.
Tip forward, lift the feet and straighten the arms.
hold: Round the upper back and engage the core.
Feet together, gaze ahead of the hands.
exit: Bend the elbows and lower the feet with control.

grue.breath: Keep the breath short but steady, never held.

accroupi-pointes.name: Toe Balance
accroupi-pointes.summary: A squat balanced on the balls of the feet, knees together, hands in prayer. It strengthens feet and ankles and refines balance.

entry: Stand and rise onto the balls of the feet.
Bend the knees and lower into a squat, heels high.
Bring the palms together at the chest.
hold: Keep the back tall and the gaze fixed.
Spread the weight across all toes.
exit: Place the hands down, lower the heels and stand up.

accroupi-pointes.breath: Keep the breath calm and even to steady the balance.

double-pigeon.name: Fire Log
double-pigeon.summary: A seated pose with the shins stacked, ankle over knee. It deeply opens the outer hips.

entry: Sit and place the left shin parallel to the front of the mat.
Stack the right shin on top, ankle over knee.
Flex both feet to protect the knees.
hold: Sit tall or fold the torso forward.
Fill gaps under the knees with blocks if needed.
exit: Lift the torso, unstack the legs and switch sides.

double-pigeon.breath: Exhale to soften the hips; breathe slowly.

heros-allonge.name: Reclining Hero
heros-allonge.summary: From Hero, recline back between the heels. It deeply stretches the quadriceps, hip flexors and abdomen.

entry: Sit in Hero between the heels.
Lean back onto the hands, then the forearms.
Lie back on the floor or a bolster.
hold: Keep the knees close, tailbone slightly tucked.
Arms by the sides or overhead.
exit: Press up onto the forearms, then the hands, and sit up.
Extend the legs one at a time.

heros-allonge.breath: Breathe into the open belly and chest.

cat-tail-pulling-pose-b.name: Cat Pulling Its Tail (B)
cat-tail-pulling-pose-b.summary: A reclined side twist where you catch the foot of the bent back leg. It combines twisting, a quad stretch and shoulder opening.

entry: Lie on the back and drop the bent knees to one side.
Keep the lower leg extended or bent; bend the top leg back.
Catch that foot with the opposite hand.
hold: Open the free shoulder toward the floor.
Stay without yanking on the foot.
exit: Release the foot, return to the back and switch sides.

cat-tail-pulling-pose-b.breath: Exhale to deepen the twist; breathe slowly.

standing-twist-straight-arms.name: Standing Twist with Straight Arms
standing-twist-straight-arms.summary: A standing torso rotation with straight arms following the movement. It mobilizes the spine and warms up the trunk.
contraindications: Herniated disc or acute back pain

entry: Stand feet hip-width apart, knees soft.
Raise straight arms to shoulder height.
Rotate the torso to one side, arms following.
hold: Keep the pelvis steady and facing forward.
Alternate sides smoothly.
exit: Return to center and lower the arms.

standing-twist-straight-arms.breath: Exhale as you twist, inhale back to center.

arbre-droit.name: Handstand
arbre-droit.summary: A full inversion balanced on the hands with the body vertical. It builds major upper-body strength, core control and balance.
contraindications: High blood pressure, glaucoma or heart condition

entry: From Down Dog, place hands shoulder-width, near a wall if needed.
Walk the feet in and lift one leg.
Hop lightly with the other leg to come up.
hold: Push the floor away, shoulders by the ears, ribs drawn in.
Legs together and active.
exit: Lower one leg at a time and rest in Child's Pose.

arbre-droit.breath: Breathe steadily; come down if the breath strains.

moon-salutation.name: Moon Salutation
moon-salutation.summary: A slow, side-to-side sequence (crescent, goddess, triangle, lunges) travelling across the mat. A gentle, cooling practice that opens the hips.
contraindications: Reduce range of motion in pregnancy

entry: Stand at the center of the mat, hands in prayer.
Side bends, then Goddess and Star.
Triangle, Pyramid and side lunges toward one side.
hold: Link each pose to the breath.
Retrace the path toward the opposite side.
exit: Finish standing at center in Mountain, hands at the heart.

moon-salutation.breath: One pose per inhale or exhale, slow and fluid breath.

eye-exercise-palming-close-up.name: Eye Exercise: Palming
eye-exercise-palming-close-up.summary: An eye-relaxation exercise: rub the palms together and cup them over closed eyes. It relaxes the eyes and calms the mind.
contraindications: Eye infection or recent eye surgery

entry: Sit comfortably with a tall spine.
Rub the palms briskly to warm them.
Cup the palms over closed eyes without pressing.
hold: Rest in the warmth and darkness for a few breaths.
exit: Slowly draw the hands away and open the eyes gently.

eye-exercise-palming-close-up.breath: Breathe slowly and deeply with a relaxed face.

posture-sur-les-avant-bras.name: Forearm Stand
posture-sur-les-avant-bras.summary: An inversion balanced on the forearms with the legs vertical. It strongly builds shoulder and core strength.

entry: From Dolphin, forearms parallel, near a wall if needed.
Walk the feet in and lift one leg.
Bring the other leg up with a small controlled hop.
hold: Press the forearms down, shoulders over elbows.
Ribs drawn in, legs active.
exit: Lower one leg at a time and rest in Child's Pose.

posture-sur-les-avant-bras.breath: Keep the breath steady throughout the balance.

supine-spinal-twist-pose-ii-bolster-unde.name: Supine Spinal Twist II with Bolster Under Legs
supine-spinal-twist-pose-ii-bolster-unde.summary: A restorative reclined twist with the bent legs resting on a bolster to the side. It releases the spine without strain.
contraindications: Herniated disc or acute back pain

entry: Place a bolster to one side, near the hips.
Lie on the back with the knees bent.
Lower the knees onto the bolster.
hold: Arms open, shoulders grounded.
Turn the head the other way if comfortable.
exit: Bring the knees back to center and switch sides.

supine-spinal-twist-pose-ii-bolster-unde.breath: Exhale to release and let the breath settle.

grand-ecart-lateral.name: Center Splits
grand-ecart-lateral.summary: Legs extended wide to the sides with the pelvis lowering toward the floor. It intensely stretches the adductors and inner thighs.

entry: Stand with legs very wide, hands on the floor or blocks.
Gradually slide the feet outward.
Lower to the forearms if possible.
hold: Kneecaps and toes toward the ceiling or forward.
Stop at a moderate stretch.
exit: Press back onto the hands and walk the feet in.

grand-ecart-lateral.breath: Exhale slowly to soften the inner thighs.

lion.name: Lion
lion.summary: A kneeling pose with a forceful exhale, mouth open and tongue out. It releases tension in the face, throat and chest.

entry: Sit on the heels, hands on the knees, fingers spread.
Inhale deeply through the nose.
Exhale strongly through the mouth, tongue toward the chin, gaze up.
hold: Repeat 2 to 4 times.
exit: Close the mouth, relax the face and breathe normally.

lion.breath: Audible "ha" exhale through the mouth, inhale through the nose.

crescent-high-lunge-pose-tricep-kickback.name: Crescent High Lunge with Triceps Kickbacks (Weights)
crescent-high-lunge-pose-tricep-kickback.summary: A high lunge with the torso hinged forward, combined with arm extensions backward using light weights. It strengthens legs and triceps while training balance.

entry: In a high lunge, front knee over ankle, a weight in each hand.
Hinge the torso forward with a long back.
Bend the elbows close to the body, weights by the ribs.
hold: Straighten the arms back, then bend the elbows again.
Repeat with elbows fixed and the lunge steady.
exit: Set the weights down, step the back foot in and switch sides.

crescent-high-lunge-pose-tricep-kickback.breath: Exhale as the arms extend, inhale as they bend.

supported-roll-up-flow.name: Supported Roll-Up Flow
supported-roll-up-flow.summary: A Pilates-style flow rolling vertebra by vertebra between lying and sitting, assisted by the hands or a strap. It strengthens the abdominals and mobilizes the spine.
benefits: Articulates the spine segment by segment
Stretches the back of the legs
contraindications: Acute back pain or herniated disc

entry: Sit with legs straight or knees bent, hands behind the thighs.
Tuck the chin and roll the back down toward the floor.
Use the hands to control the descent.
hold: Roll back up, chin then shoulders, to sitting.
Repeat slowly several times.
exit: Finish seated with a long spine, or lying at rest.

supported-roll-up-flow.breath: Exhale as you roll, inhale at the top or bottom.

half-squat-pose-prayer-hands.name: Half Squat with Prayer Hands
half-squat-pose-prayer-hands.summary: A deep side lunge with one leg bent and the other straight to the side, palms together at the chest. It opens hips and inner thighs and strengthens the legs.

entry: Stand with legs wide, toes slightly turned out.
Bend one knee and shift the hips toward that side.
Straighten the other leg, toes up, hands in prayer.
hold: Torso upright, elbows gently pressing the inner knee.
Heel of the bent leg down if possible.
exit: Rise to center and switch sides.

half-squat-pose-prayer-hands.breath: Breathe slowly into the inner thighs.

reclining-hero-pose-variation-one-leg-st.name: Reclining Hero, One Leg Straight, Head on Bolster
reclining-hero-pose-variation-one-leg-st.summary: A gentler Reclining Hero: one leg folded in Hero, the other straight, the back and head resting on a bolster. It stretches the quad one side at a time.
benefits: Stretches quad and psoas on one side

entry: Place a bolster lengthwise behind you.
Sit with one leg folded in Hero and the other straight.
Recline onto the bolster with the head supported.
hold: Keep the bent knee near the midline, not drifting out.
Arms relaxed by the sides.
exit: Press up onto the forearms, then the hands, and switch legs.

reclining-hero-pose-variation-one-leg-st.breath: Breathe fully into the front of the hip.

revolved-low-lunge-arm-circling.name: Revolved Low Lunge with Arm Circles
revolved-low-lunge-arm-circling.summary: A low lunge with a torso twist, the top arm drawing large circles. It mobilizes shoulders and spine while opening the hip.
contraindications: Knee injury: pad the back knee

entry: In a low lunge, back knee down, opposite hand on the floor by the front foot.
Rotate the torso toward the front leg.
Reach the other arm up.
hold: Draw large, slow circles with the raised arm.
Keep the pelvis steady and the gaze following the hand.
exit: Lower the hand, return to center and switch sides.

revolved-low-lunge-arm-circling.breath: Inhale as the arm opens, exhale as it returns.

alternate-nostril-breathing-close-up.name: Alternate Nostril Breathing
alternate-nostril-breathing-close-up.summary: A pranayama technique alternating the breath between nostrils, closing them with the fingers. It balances and calms the mind.
contraindications: Never force or hold the breath without guidance

entry: Sit comfortably with a tall spine.
Right hand: fold index and middle fingers, thumb and ring finger ready.
Close the right nostril with the thumb and inhale through the left.
hold: Close the left, exhale right, inhale right, then switch.
Continue several rounds at a slow pace.
exit: Finish with an exhale through the left, lower the hand and breathe freely.

alternate-nostril-breathing-close-up.breath: Slow, quiet, even breath on each side.

banana-pose-aerial.name: Aerial Banana
banana-pose-aerial.summary: A reclined side stretch, the body curved like a banana, supported by the aerial hammock. It opens the whole side body.

entry: With the hammock low, lie on the back in the fabric or on the floor beneath it, depending on the variation.
Walk feet and hands toward the same side.
Curve the body into an arc, arms overhead.
hold: Let the opposite side body lengthen.
Cross the ankles or wrists to deepen.
exit: Return the body to center and switch sides.

banana-pose-aerial.breath: Breathe into the stretched side, ribs expanding.

heart-chakra.name: Heart Chakra
heart-chakra.summary: Not a pose: this item represents the heart chakra (Anahata), used as a class theme or intention around openness, compassion and connection.

jambe-derriere-tete.name: Foot Behind the Head
jambe-derriere-tete.summary: An advanced seated pose with one leg placed behind the head, the other extended. It requires very deep hip opening and a strong spine.

entry: Sit and warm up the hips thoroughly.
Cradle the right leg against the chest.
Slide the shoulder under the knee and bring the foot behind the head.
hold: Lift the head and torso to hold the leg in place.
Hands in prayer at the chest.
exit: Release the leg slowly with the hands and switch sides.

jambe-derriere-tete.breath: Slow breathing; release if the breath gets short.

constructive-rest-bridge-pose-flow.name: Constructive Rest to Bridge Flow
constructive-rest-bridge-pose-flow.summary: A gentle flow between Constructive Rest (lying, knees bent) and Bridge, guided by the breath. It mobilizes the spine and wakes up glutes and back.
benefits: Articulates the spine vertebra by vertebra

entry: Lie on the back, knees bent, feet hip-width.
Arms by the sides, palms down.
Settle for a few breaths in Constructive Rest.
hold: Inhale and peel the hips up into Bridge.
Exhale and roll down vertebra by vertebra; repeat.
exit: Return to Constructive Rest, knees resting together.

constructive-rest-bridge-pose-flow.breath: Inhale to lift, exhale to lower.

half-reverse-pigeon-pose-variation-foot-.name: Half Reverse Pigeon with Foot on Block
half-reverse-pigeon-pose-variation-foot-.summary: A reclined pose with one ankle crossed over the opposite thigh and the other foot resting on a block. It gently stretches the glutes and piriformis.

entry: Lie on the back, knees bent, one foot on a block.
Cross the other ankle over the thigh, foot flexed.
Let the crossed knee open.
hold: Adjust the block height to tune the stretch.
Keep the pelvis grounded and shoulders relaxed.
exit: Uncross the leg and switch sides.

half-reverse-pigeon-pose-variation-foot-.breath: Exhale to soften the hip; breathe slowly.

head-to-knee-wild-thing-pose-knee-on-flo.name: Head-to-Knee to Wild Thing Flow (Knee Down)
head-to-knee-wild-thing-pose-knee-on-flo.summary: A flow between a Head-to-Knee forward fold and a knee-down Wild Thing that opens the chest. It alternates a hamstring stretch with heart opening.

entry: Sit in Head-to-Knee, one leg straight, the other bent.
Exhale and fold over the straight leg.
Place one hand behind you to prepare the transition.
hold: Inhale: press into the hand, lift the hips, knee down, free arm reaching back.
Exhale: return to the fold; repeat.
exit: Return to sitting and switch sides.

head-to-knee-wild-thing-pose-knee-on-flo.breath: Exhale into the fold, inhale into the opening.

wide-legged-standing-backbend-pose-hands.name: Wide-Legged Standing Backbend, Hands Clasped Behind
wide-legged-standing-backbend-pose-hands.summary: A standing backbend with legs wide and fingers interlaced behind the back. It opens chest and shoulders from a stable base.

entry: Stand with legs wide, feet parallel.
Interlace the fingers behind the back.
Inhale, lift the chest and draw the arms down and back.
hold: Lift the chest without crunching the lower back.
Neck long, legs active.
exit: Return upright and release the hands.

wide-legged-standing-backbend-pose-hands.breath: Inhale to open, then breathe steadily.

cat-pose-twist-hands-side.name: Cat Twist with Hands to the Side
cat-pose-twist-hands-side.summary: A tabletop Cat variation with the hands walked to one side, adding a twist to the rounded back. It mobilizes the spine and side body.
benefits: Stretches upper back and side body

entry: Come to all fours, knees under hips.
Walk both hands toward one side of the mat.
Exhale and round the back, gaze toward the navel.
hold: Feel the stretch along the opposite side.
Keep hips over knees.
exit: Walk the hands back to center and switch sides.

cat-pose-twist-hands-side.breath: Exhale as you round the back.

prone-tree-pose.name: Prone Tree
prone-tree-pose.summary: A reclined Tree variation lying face down, one knee bent out to the side, sole against the opposite leg. It gently opens the hip without any balance challenge.
benefits: Opens the hip in external rotation

entry: Lie on the belly, forehead on the hands.
Bend one knee and slide it out to the side.
Place the sole against the inner straight leg.
hold: Let the pelvis settle into the floor.
Relax shoulders and face.
exit: Straighten the leg and switch sides.

prone-tree-pose.breath: Breathe into the belly against the floor.

cow-pose-twist-hands-side.name: Cow Twist with Hands to the Side
cow-pose-twist-hands-side.summary: A tabletop Cow variation with the hands walked to one side, combining back extension and twist. It opens the chest and mobilizes the side body.

entry: Come to all fours, knees under hips.
Walk both hands toward one side of the mat.
Inhale, drop the belly and lift the chest, gaze forward.
hold: Feel the opening along the side body.
Keep the neck long.
exit: Walk the hands back to center and switch sides.

reclined-big-toe-pose-variation-i-head-t.name: Reclined Big Toe, Head to Knee
reclined-big-toe-pose-variation-i-head-t.summary: Lying on the back, you hold the foot of a raised leg and draw the forehead toward the knee. It combines a hamstring stretch with core work.

entry: Lie on the back and lift the right leg.
Hold the big toe or use a strap.
Exhale and curl head and shoulders toward the knee.
hold: Keep the grounded leg active, foot flexed.
Relax the neck; don't force contact.
exit: Lower head and shoulders, then the leg, and switch sides.

reclined-big-toe-pose-variation-i-head-t.breath: Exhale as you curl toward the knee.

toe-balance-palm-tree-pose-tiptoes-flow.name: Toe Balance to Palm Tree on Tiptoes Flow
toe-balance-palm-tree-pose-tiptoes-flow.summary: A flow between a squat on the balls of the feet and Palm Tree, standing on tiptoes with arms overhead. It strengthens feet and legs and refines balance.

entry: Stand with feet together or hip-width.
Inhale: rise onto tiptoes, arms straight overhead.
Exhale: lower into a squat on the toes, hands in prayer.
hold: Repeat several times while staying on the toes.
Fix the gaze to hold balance.
exit: Lower the heels and return to Mountain.

toe-balance-palm-tree-pose-tiptoes-flow.breath: Inhale to rise, exhale to lower.

eight-limbed-pose-flow-variation.name: Eight-Limbed Pose Flow Variation
eight-limbed-pose-flow-variation.summary: A flow built around Eight-Limbed Pose (knees, chest and chin down, hips lifted), often used in Sun Salutations. It strengthens the arms and prepares for backbends.

entry: From plank, lower the knees.
Exhale: lower chest and chin between the hands, hips high.
Keep the elbows hugging the body.
hold: Inhale: slide forward into Cobra.
Exhale: return to Down Dog or all fours; repeat.
exit: Finish in Child's Pose or Downward-Facing Dog.

eight-limbed-pose-flow-variation.breath: Exhale to lower, inhale to open into Cobra.

supported-wide-legs-up-the-wall-blocks-b.name: Supported Wide-Legged Legs Up the Wall (Blocks and Bolster)
supported-wide-legs-up-the-wall-blocks-b.summary: A restorative Legs Up the Wall with the legs open in a V, pelvis on a bolster and thighs supported by blocks. It gently opens the groin and calms.
benefits: Gently opens inner thighs and groin

entry: Place a bolster near the wall and a block on each side.
Sit sideways, then lie back and swing the legs up, pelvis on the bolster.
Open the legs into a V and rest the outer thighs on the blocks.
hold: Relax the arms and close the eyes.
Stay several minutes with no strain in the groin.
exit: Bring the legs together, bend the knees, slide off the bolster and roll to the side.

supported-wide-legs-up-the-wall-blocks-b.breath: Slow, natural breath with a soft belly.

wide-legged-child-pose-arms-wide-head-si.name: Wide-Knee Child's Pose, Arms Wide, Head to the Side
wide-legged-child-pose-arms-wide-head-si.summary: A resting kneeling pose with knees wide, arms spread out to the sides and one cheek on the floor. It releases back, hips and shoulders.
benefits: Stretches the chest on one side

entry: Kneel with big toes together, knees wide.
Sit toward the heels and lower the torso between the thighs.
Spread the arms to the sides and rest one cheek down.
hold: Let the body weight sink into the floor.
Turn the head to the other side halfway through.
exit: Bring the arms in, rise to all fours or sit on the heels.

reclined-butterfly-blocks-strap-blanket.name: Reclined Butterfly (Blocks, Strap, Blanket)
reclined-butterfly-blocks-strap-blanket.summary: A restorative reclined pose, soles together and knees open, supported by blocks under the thighs, a strap around hips and feet and a blanket. It opens the hips and invites deep rest.

entry: Set up the blocks, a strap looped around hips and feet, and a blanket.
Bring the soles together and lie back.
Rest the outer thighs on blocks; blanket under the head or over the body.
hold: Adjust the strap so the feet stay close without strain.
Relax the arms and close the eyes.
exit: Remove the strap, bring the knees together with the hands and roll to one side.

seated-forward-bend-pose-feet-aerial.name: Aerial Seated Forward Bend, Feet in Hammock
seated-forward-bend-pose-feet-aerial.summary: A seated forward fold with the feet resting in a suspended aerial hammock. The hammock lifts the legs and deepens the back-body stretch.

entry: With the hammock low, sit facing it.
Rest heels or calves in the fabric, legs straight.
Inhale to lengthen the spine.
hold: Exhale and hinge forward, hands toward the legs or fabric.
Keep the back long rather than rounding.
exit: Inhale to lift the torso, then remove the feet from the hammock.

seated-forward-bend-pose-feet-aerial.breath: Exhale to fold and breathe slowly into the stretch.

revolved-curtsy-lunge-pose-arms-out.name: Revolved Curtsy Lunge, Arms Out
revolved-curtsy-lunge-pose-arms-out.summary: A lunge with the back leg crossing behind the front leg like a curtsy, plus a torso twist with arms open. It strengthens the legs and trains balance and rotation.
contraindications: Balance issues: stay near a wall

entry: Stand and cross the right leg behind the left.
Bend both knees, front knee over ankle.
Open the arms to shoulder height and twist toward the front leg.
hold: Keep the pelvis steady and arms active.
Gaze toward the back hand if comfortable.
exit: Return to center, bring the feet together and switch sides.

revolved-curtsy-lunge-pose-arms-out.breath: Exhale into the twist and breathe steadily.

revolved-triangle-pose-hand-chair.name: Revolved Triangle, Hand on Chair
revolved-triangle-pose-hand-chair.summary: Revolved Triangle with the lower hand resting on the seat of a chair. It makes the twist accessible while keeping the spine long.
contraindications: Unstable chair: brace it against a wall

entry: Place a chair in front of you, by the front foot.
Feet a leg's length apart, hips facing forward.
Hinge forward and place the opposite hand on the seat.
hold: Twist the torso and reach the other arm up.
Keep the spine long and legs active.
exit: Lower the arm, rise up and switch sides.

revolved-triangle-pose-hand-chair.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to twist.

standing-fish-pose-block-head-wall.name: Standing Fish, Block Between Head and Wall
standing-fish-pose-block-head-wall.summary: A standing backbend with the back to the wall and the back of the head supported by a block against it. It opens the chest safely.

entry: Stand with your back to the wall, a step away.
Place a block between the back of the head and the wall.
Lift the sternum and open the chest, hands on the hips.
hold: Let the block support the head without crunching the neck.
Legs active, hips over feet.
exit: Bring the torso upright and remove the block.

standing-cross-crawl-pose-elbow-knee-blo.name: Standing Cross Crawl, Elbow to Knee, Block
standing-cross-crawl-pose-elbow-knee-blo.summary: A dynamic standing exercise bringing the elbow to the opposite knee, with a block used as a target or hold. It trains coordination, core and balance.
contraindications: Balance issues: stay near a wall

entry: Stand feet hip-width, a block within reach as the variation requires.
Raise the arms overhead.
Lift the right knee and draw the left elbow toward it.
hold: Alternate sides at a steady pace.
Keep the torso long and core engaged.
exit: Return to Mountain, arms by the sides.

standing-cross-crawl-pose-elbow-knee-blo.breath: Exhale as elbow and knee meet.

cloud-hands.name: Cloud Hands
cloud-hands.summary: A slow, circular hand movement in front of the body, drawn from tai chi, with a gentle weight shift from leg to leg. It calms the mind and mobilizes shoulders and waist.

entry: Stand with feet slightly wider than hips, knees soft.
One hand at face height, the other in front of the belly, palms facing you.
Turn the torso gently, gliding the hands like clouds.
hold: Switch hand positions on each pass.
Shift the weight smoothly.
exit: Slow down, bring the hands in front of the belly and rest still.

cloud-hands.breath: Slow, continuous breath matched to the movement.

revolved-shoelace-pose-side-stretch.name: Revolved Shoelace with Side Stretch
revolved-shoelace-pose-side-stretch.summary: A seated pose with stacked knees (Cow Face legs), combined with a side bend and torso rotation. It opens the hips and stretches the side body.

entry: Sit and cross the legs, stacking the knees, feet to either side.
Place one hand on the floor beside the hip.
Raise the other arm and bend sideways, turning the chest slightly.
hold: Keep both sit bones grounded if possible.
Lengthen the side body with each inhale.
exit: Return to center, uncross and switch legs and sides.

revolved-shoelace-pose-side-stretch.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to bend.

cradle-pose-hips-floor-feet-raised-aeria.name: Aerial Cradle, Hips on Floor, Feet Raised
cradle-pose-hips-floor-feet-raised-aeria.summary: Lying or seated with the pelvis on the floor and the feet or legs resting in a suspended aerial hammock. A restorative variation that relieves legs and back.
contraindications: Glaucoma or uncontrolled high blood pressure

entry: Set the hammock low.
Lie on the back, pelvis on the floor near the hammock.
Rest the calves or feet in the fabric.
hold: Relax the arms and let the hammock hold the legs.
Option: gentle swaying.
exit: Take the feet out, bend the knees and roll to one side.

foot-behind-head-pose-prep-big-toe-varia.name: Foot Behind Head Prep, Big Toe Hold
foot-behind-head-pose-prep-big-toe-varia.summary: A reclined preparation holding the big toe and guiding the bent leg outside the shoulder. It progressively opens the hip before the full pose.

entry: Lie on the back and bend the right leg.
Hold the right big toe with the right hand.
Guide the knee outward and the foot toward the head.
hold: Keep the other leg grounded and the pelvis steady.
Progress gradually without forcing the knee.
exit: Release the foot, extend the leg and switch sides.

foot-behind-head-pose-prep-big-toe-varia.breath: Breathe slowly; ease off at any knee strain.

seated-upward-salute-side-bend-pose-hand.name: Seated Upward Salute Side Bend with Strap (Chair)
seated-upward-salute-side-bend-pose-hand.summary: Seated on a chair, arms raised holding a taut strap, you bend to the side. It stretches the side body and opens the shoulders with full stability.

entry: Sit at the edge of a chair, feet flat.
Hold a strap, hands wider than shoulders.
Raise the arms overhead, keeping the strap taut.
hold: Exhale and bend to one side.
Keep both sit bones on the chair.
exit: Inhale back to center, switch sides, then lower the arms.

seated-upward-salute-side-bend-pose-hand.breath: Inhale at center, exhale to bend.

one-arm-reverse-table-top-pose.name: One-Arm Reverse Tabletop
one-arm-reverse-table-top-pose.summary: Reverse Tabletop (hands and feet down, hips lifted, facing up) with one arm reaching overhead. It strengthens arms and glutes and opens the chest.
contraindications: Neck issues: keep the chin tucked

entry: Sit with knees bent, feet down, hands behind the hips.
Lift the hips to knee height.
Shift weight onto one hand and reach the other arm overhead.
hold: Keep the hips high and knees parallel.
Press actively through the grounded hand.
exit: Lower the hand, lower the hips and switch sides.

one-arm-reverse-table-top-pose.breath: Inhale as the arm lifts, then breathe steadily.

side-lying-pose-rib-cage-mobility.name: Side-Lying Rib Cage Mobility
side-lying-pose-rib-cage-mobility.summary: A gentle side-lying exercise, knees bent, in which the top arm opens and closes to mobilize the ribs and upper spine.
benefits: Mobilizes rib cage and upper spine

entry: Lie on the side, knees bent to hip height, head supported.
Extend the arms forward, palms together.
Arc the top arm open behind you, eyes following the hand.
hold: Close the arm back; repeat slowly.
Keep the knees stacked.
exit: Bring the arm back and switch sides.

side-lying-pose-rib-cage-mobility.breath: Inhale to open, exhale to close.

standing-half-splits-pose.name: Standing Splits
standing-half-splits-pose.summary: A standing forward fold on one straight leg with the other lifted back, hands on the floor or blocks. It stretches the hamstrings and trains balance.

entry: From a standing forward fold, hands on the floor or blocks.
Shift weight onto one leg.
Lift the other leg straight back.
hold: Hips level or allowed to open, per the variation.
Head releasing toward the standing leg.
exit: Lower the leg and switch sides.

pendant-pose-hands-chair-one-foot-block.name: Pendant Prep, Hands on Chair, One Foot on Block
pendant-pose-hands-chair-one-foot-block.summary: An adapted Pendant preparation: hands on a chair, lifting part of the body weight while one foot stays on a block. It builds arm and core strength progressively.
contraindications: Unstable chair: brace against a wall

entry: Set a stable chair and a block in front.
Hands on the seat, one foot on the block.
Press into the hands and lighten the standing foot.
hold: Draw the belly in and round the back slightly.
Keep the other knee drawn toward the chest.
exit: Return weight to the foot and switch legs.

pendant-pose-hands-chair-one-foot-block.breath: Exhale to lift and keep breathing.

twisted-frog-pose.name: Twisted Frog
twisted-frog-pose.summary: Lying face down, you bend one knee and hold the foot near the hip while rotating the torso. It stretches the quads and hip flexors with a gentle twist.

entry: Lie on the belly, propped on the left forearm.
Bend the right knee and hold the right foot with the right hand.
Draw the heel toward the hip and turn the chest to the left.
hold: Keep the hips grounded.
Press the foot down without straining the knee.
exit: Release the foot, lie down and switch sides.

twisted-frog-pose.breath: Breathe into the front thigh and chest.

revolved-downward-facing-hero-pose-exten.name: Revolved Downward-Facing Hero Flow, Hands Extended
revolved-downward-facing-hero-pose-exten.summary: A flow from a knees-together Child's Pose with arms extended, walking the hands side to side to create a twist. It stretches the back, shoulders and side body.

entry: Kneel, sit toward the heels and extend the torso forward.
Reach the arms forward, forehead down.
Walk the hands toward one side of the mat.
hold: Thread one arm under the other to twist, then return to center.
Alternate sides with the breath.
exit: Bring the hands to center and rise slowly.
