jambes-au-mur-papillon.description: Buttocks against the wall, bend the knees and bring the soles of the feet together, letting them slide down the wall.

inversion-sur-bloc.name: Supported Inversion on a Block
inversion-sur-bloc.description: Lying down with a block under the sacrum, raise the straight legs toward the sky and let the pelvis rest heavily on the support.

yin-papillon.name: Butterfly (Yin)
yin-papillon.description: Soles of the feet together fairly far in front of the pelvis, knees open, back rounding toward the feet without forcing. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, with a cushion under the buttocks and blocks under the knees if needed.

yin-demi-papillon.name: Half Butterfly
yin-demi-papillon.description: One leg extended, the other foot against the inner thigh, the torso folding over the straight leg or the center. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, with a cushion under the pelvis and the straight knee slightly bent.
benefits: Stretches the back of the leg and the back

yin-demi-papillon-lateral.name: Half Butterfly Side Bend
yin-demi-papillon-lateral.description: From Half Butterfly, lean sideways toward the straight leg with the elbow or hand on a block, the other arm reaching over the ear. Hold for 2 to 4 minutes per side.
benefits: Stretches the whole side body and ribs
contraindications: Shoulder pain (keep the hand on the head)

yin-chenille.name: Caterpillar
yin-chenille.description: Seated with legs extended, let the back round and the torso fold over the legs without trying to reach the feet. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, with a cushion under the buttocks and a bolster on the thighs or under the knees.
benefits: Gently stretches the entire back body

yin-selle.name: Saddle
yin-selle.description: Sitting between or on the heels, lower the back onto a bolster or onto the elbows, letting the lower back arch gently. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes and come out slowly by pressing up onto the elbows.
benefits: Stretches the quadriceps and hip flexors
Stimulates the lumbar and sacral area

yin-demi-selle.name: Half Saddle
yin-demi-selle.description: One leg folded with the foot beside the hip, the other leg extended or foot on the floor; lean back onto the elbows or a bolster. Hold for 3 minutes per side.
benefits: Stretches one quadriceps at a time
A more accessible version of Saddle
Opens the front of the hip

yin-dragon.name: Baby Dragon
yin-dragon.description: Lunge with the back knee down, hands on either side of the front foot, pelvis sinking slowly toward the floor. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes, with a blanket under the back knee and blocks under the hands.
benefits: Opens the front of the back hip
Stretches the groin of the front leg

yin-dragon-haut.name: Dragon Flying High
yin-dragon-haut.description: From Dragon, lift the torso and place the hands on the front knee; the weight shifts forward to stretch the back hip flexor. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes, with a blanket under the knee.
benefits: Intensely stretches the psoas of the back leg
contraindications: Lower back pain if the arch deepens

yin-dragon-bas.name: Dragon Flying Low
yin-dragon-bas.description: From Dragon, place both hands inside the front foot, then lower onto the forearms, using a bolster or blocks if the floor feels far. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes.
benefits: Deeply opens the groin and front hip

yin-dragon-aile.name: Winged Dragon
yin-dragon-aile.description: From Dragon Flying Low, let the front knee fall open and the foot roll onto its outer edge, hands or forearms inside. Hold for 1 to 2 minutes, with blocks under the hands.
benefits: Opens the hip in external rotation
Stretches the inner thigh of the front leg

yin-dragon-tourne.name: Twisted Dragon
yin-dragon-tourne.description: From Dragon, keep the opposite hand on the floor and turn the torso toward the front leg, the other arm opening toward the ceiling or reaching for the back foot. Hold for 1 to 2 minutes, with a block under the supporting hand.
benefits: Stretches the quadriceps if you hold the back foot

yin-dragon-pont.name: Overpass Dragon
yin-dragon-pont.description: From Dragon, lift the back knee off the floor and lengthen the back leg, hands on either side of the front foot. Hold for 1 to 2 minutes, with blocks under the hands.
benefits: Intensely stretches the back hip flexor
contraindications: Fatigue in the arms or wrists

yin-dragon-grand-ecart.name: Dragon Splits
yin-dragon-grand-ecart.description: From Dragon, slide the front foot forward and the back leg back to the edge of your split, pelvis supported by a bolster, hands on blocks. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and hip flexors
Calls for patience and letting go

yin-phoque.name: Seal
yin-phoque.description: Lying on the belly, hands in front and slightly apart, arms straight; the torso lifts while the buttocks stay relaxed. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes, hands on blocks to adjust the intensity.
benefits: Compresses and stimulates the lower back
A more intense version of Sphinx

yin-sphinx.name: Yin Sphinx
yin-sphinx.description: Lying on the belly, elbows slightly in front of the shoulders, forearms parallel; let the belly and glutes relax. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, with a bolster under the armpits to soften it.
benefits: Passive backbend for the lower back

yin-lacet.name: Shoelace
yin-lacet.description: Seated with one knee stacked over the other and the feet on either side of the hips, then let the torso round forward. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, with a cushion under the buttocks to keep both sit bones grounded.
benefits: Deeply stretches the glutes and outer hip

yin-demi-lacet.name: Half Shoelace
yin-demi-lacet.description: One leg extended in front, the other crossed over it with the foot outside the straight thigh; the torso leans gently forward. Hold for 3 minutes per side, with a cushion under the buttocks.
benefits: Stretches the back of the straight leg

yin-cerf.name: Deer
yin-cerf.description: Seated, one leg bent in front in external rotation, the other bent to the side with the foot pointing back, both knees at right angles. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, torso upright or folding over the front leg, with a cushion under the hip if needed.
benefits: Mobilizes the hips in internal and external rotation
contraindications: Knee injury (bring the back foot closer)

yin-cerf-torsion.name: Twisted Deer
yin-cerf-torsion.description: From Deer, turn the torso toward the back leg and lie down over a bolster or place the hands on the floor. Hold for 2 to 4 minutes per side.

yin-carre.name: Square
yin-carre.description: Seated with the shins stacked and parallel to the front edge of the mat, top ankle over the bottom knee, then fold forward if you like. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, with a blanket between knee and ankle if there is a gap.
benefits: Intensely opens the hip in external rotation
contraindications: Knee injury (choose Shoelace or Deer instead)

yin-escargot.name: Snail
yin-escargot.description: From lying on your back, bring the legs over the head, feet on the floor or on a block behind you, knees bending toward the ears if needed. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes, with a folded blanket under the shoulders to protect the neck.
benefits: Stretches the whole spine and neck

yin-libellule.name: Dragonfly (Yin)
yin-libellule.description: Seated with the legs wide apart, let the torso move forward and the back round, hands on the floor or on a bolster. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, with a cushion under the buttocks and the knees slightly bent.
benefits: Stretches the inner thighs and hamstrings

yin-libellule-laterale.name: Dragonfly Side Bend
yin-libellule-laterale.description: From Dragonfly, lean sideways toward one leg, elbow on a block or on the thigh, the other arm overhead. Hold for 2 to 3 minutes per side.
benefits: Stretches the side body and intercostals

yin-chat-queue.name: Cat Pulling Its Tail
yin-chat-queue.description: Lying in a twist, top knee drawn toward the chest, the other leg bent behind you: the free hand catches the back foot. Hold for 2 to 4 minutes, with a cushion under the top knee.
benefits: Combines a twist with a quadriceps stretch
Opens the front of the hip

yin-cygne.name: Swan
yin-cygne.description: Front shin angled in front of the pelvis, back leg extended, hands on the floor with straight arms to keep the torso lifted. Hold for 1 to 2 minutes before lowering into Sleeping Swan, with a cushion under the front hip.
benefits: Opens the front hip and the back-leg psoas

yin-cygne-endormi.name: Sleeping Swan
yin-cygne-endormi.description: From Swan, fold the torso forward onto the forearms with a bolster or cushion under the forehead, and let the pelvis grow heavy. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, with a blanket under the front hip.
benefits: Releases the glutes and lower back
contraindications: Knee injury (choose Reclined Figure Four instead)

yin-coeur-qui-fond.name: Melting Heart
yin-coeur-qui-fond.description: On all fours with hips over knees, walk the hands forward and let the chest sink toward the floor, forehead or chin down. Hold for 2 to 4 minutes, with a blanket under the knees and a bolster under the chest if needed.
benefits: Opens the shoulders and upper back

yin-orteils-replies.name: Toe Squat
yin-orteils-replies.description: Sitting on the heels with the toes tucked under, making sure the little toes are tucked too. Hold for only 1 to 2 minutes, often just before Ankle Stretch.
benefits: Stimulates the meridians of the feet
Trains you to stay present with intensity

yin-chevilles.name: Ankle Stretch
yin-chevilles.description: Sitting on the heels with the tops of the feet on the floor, lean back onto the hands and gently lift the knees to stretch the top of the foot. Hold for 1 to 2 minutes, with a rolled blanket under the ankles.
benefits: Stretches the front of the ankles and shins

yin-racine-tordue.name: Twisted Root
yin-racine-tordue.description: Lying on your back, cross one thigh over the other, then let the knees drop to the opposite side, arms open on the floor. Hold for 2 to 4 minutes, with a cushion under the knees.
benefits: Calms the body before final relaxation

yin-libellule-au-mur.name: Dragonfly at the Wall
yin-libellule-au-mur.description: Lying down with the buttocks near the wall, rest the legs up the wall, then open them into a V that gravity gradually widens. Hold for 3 to 5 minutes, with cushions under the thighs if the stretch is too strong.

yin-suspendu.name: Dangling (Yin)
yin-suspendu.description: Standing with feet hip-width apart and soft knees, let the torso hang toward the floor and hold opposite elbows. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes and come up very slowly, rolling up through the spine.
benefits: Stretches the backs of the legs

yin-epaule-ventre.name: Prone Shoulder Opener
yin-epaule-ventre.description: Lying on the belly, one arm extended to the side at shoulder height, palm down; gently roll toward that arm, placing the opposite foot behind you and the free hand in front of the chest. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes per side, with a cushion under the head.
benefits: Stretches the front of the shoulder and the chest
Counteracts long hours sitting at a screen
contraindications: Tingling in the hand (reduce the range)

med-tailleur-coussin.name: Cross-Legged Seat on a Cushion
med-tailleur-coussin.description: Sitting on the front edge of a meditation cushion, legs crossed, knees lower than the hips, spine upright and hands resting. Hold for the length of your meditation, with blankets under the knees if they stay lifted.
benefits: A stable position for long meditation
contraindications: Knee injury (choose a chair or a bench)

med-birmane.name: Burmese Pose
med-birmane.description: Sitting on a cushion, both legs folded flat in front of you, one foot in front of the other without crossing, knees on the floor. Hold for 5 to 20 minutes in meditation, with a blanket under the ankles.
benefits: Easier on the knees than a cross-legged seat

med-demi-lotus.name: Half Lotus
med-demi-lotus.description: Sitting on a cushion, one foot resting on the opposite thigh near the groin, the other foot under the opposite knee, spine upright. Hold for the length of your meditation and alternate the top foot from one session to the next.
benefits: A very stable seat for meditation
contraindications: Very tight hips (never force the knee)

med-banc.name: Kneeling on a Meditation Bench
med-banc.description: Kneeling with shins on the floor, the pelvis resting on a small slanted bench placed over the ankles, spine upright. Hold for 10 to 30 minutes, with a blanket under the knees and feet.
benefits: Easier on the knees and ankles than seiza

med-seiza.name: Seiza on a Cushion
med-seiza.description: Kneeling with a cushion stood upright between the heels to sit on, knees together, hands on the thighs. Hold for 5 to 20 minutes, with a blanket under the shins.
benefits: Less pressure on the ankles than sitting on the heels

med-chaise.name: Seated Meditation on a Chair
med-chaise.description: Sitting toward the front of a chair, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, knees at right angles, back away from the backrest, hands on the thighs. Hold for the length of your meditation, with a cushion under the feet if they don't reach the floor.

med-dos-au-mur.name: Seated Against the Wall
med-dos-au-mur.description: Sitting on a cushion with the back and the back of the pelvis leaning against a wall, knees bent or legs crossed. Hold for the length of your meditation or breathing practice, with a small cushion between the wall and the lower back.
benefits: Supports the back during a long sit
Helpful when tired or with lower back pain

med-respiration-allongee.name: Constructive Rest
med-respiration-allongee.description: Lying on your back, feet flat on the floor mat-width apart, knees resting against each other, one hand on the belly. Stay for 3 to 10 minutes observing the breath, with a folded blanket under the head.
benefits: Releases the lower back and psoas
Brings calm at the start of class

mudra-jnana.name: Jnana Mudra (Seated)
mudra-jnana.description: Seated in a meditation posture, thumb and index finger touch, the other fingers extended, hands resting on the knees with palms facing up. Hold for the length of your meditation, with a cushion under the pelvis.

mudra-chin.name: Chin Mudra (Seated)
mudra-chin.description: Seated in a meditation posture, thumb and index finger touch, hands resting on the thighs with palms facing down. Hold for the length of your meditation, with a cushion under the pelvis.
benefits: A more grounding gesture than Jnana mudra

mudra-dhyana.name: Dhyana Mudra (Seated)
mudra-dhyana.description: Seated in a meditation posture, hands cupped in the lap, right hand resting in the left, thumbs lightly touching. Hold for the length of your meditation, with a cushion or blanket under the hands if the shoulders pull.
benefits: The thumbs signal when attention drifts

mudra-anjali.name: Anjali Mudra (Seated)
mudra-anjali.description: Seated, palms pressed together in front of the sternum, thumbs lightly touching the chest, elbows relaxed. Hold for a few breaths at the start or end of practice, no props needed.
benefits: Marks an intention or a greeting
Balances both sides of the body

mudra-prana.name: Prana Mudra (Seated)
mudra-prana.description: Seated in a meditation posture, tips of the thumb, ring finger and little finger joined, index and middle fingers extended, hands on the knees. Hold for 5 to 15 minutes, with a cushion under the pelvis.
benefits: Helps you stay alert in meditation

mudra-apana.name: Apana Mudra (Seated)
mudra-apana.description: Seated in a meditation posture, tips of the thumb, middle finger and ring finger joined, index and little fingers extended, hands on the knees. Hold for 5 to 15 minutes, with a cushion under the pelvis.
benefits: Traditionally associated with elimination and letting go

mudra-adi.name: Adi Mudra (Seated)
mudra-adi.description: Seated, thumb folded into the palm and wrapped by the other fingers in a soft fist, hands resting on the thighs with palms down. Hold for a few minutes before meditation or pranayama, with a cushion under the pelvis.
benefits: Directs the breath into the lower belly

mudra-bhairava.name: Bhairava Mudra (Seated)
mudra-bhairava.description: Seated in a meditation posture, right hand resting palm up in the left hand, both hands at rest in the lap. Hold for the length of your meditation, with a blanket over the thighs to support the hands.
benefits: Symbolically unites both sides of the body

mudra-prithvi.name: Prithvi Mudra (Seated)
mudra-prithvi.description: Seated in a meditation posture, tips of the thumb and ring finger joined, other fingers extended, hands resting on the knees. Hold for 5 to 15 minutes, with a cushion under the pelvis.
benefits: Associated with the earth element and stability

mudra-shanmukhi.name: Shanmukhi Mudra (Seated)
mudra-shanmukhi.description: Seated, elbows open at shoulder height, thumbs on the ears, index fingers on the closed eyelids, middle fingers along the nose and the other fingers around the mouth. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes, elbows resting on cushions if the shoulders tire.

resp-alternee.name: Alternate Nostril Breathing
resp-alternee.description: Seated in a meditation posture, the right hand in Vishnu mudra near the nose closes one nostril and then the other with each cycle, the other hand on the knee. Practice for 3 to 10 minutes, with the elbow supported on a cushion if the arm tires.
benefits: Balances and soothes the nervous system

resp-abeille.name: Bee Breath
resp-abeille.description: Seated, thumbs gently closing the ears, elbows open; exhale slowly with the mouth closed, making a low humming sound. Practice 5 to 10 rounds, hands on the knees if the shoulders tire.

montagne.summary: The reference pose for all standing poses: you stand still, rooted into the ground and lengthening toward the sky. Simple as it looks, it teaches you to distribute your weight, position the pelvis and breathe without tension. Ideal for opening a class, returning to center between two sequences or observing your everyday posture.
montagne.typicalHold: 5 to 10 breaths, or longer at the start of class

entry: Stand with your feet parallel, hip-width apart (or big toes touching).
Spread your toes, then set them down and feel the four corners of each foot.
Gently engage the thighs without locking the knees.
Let the tailbone drop gently, belly soft, lower ribs drawing down.
Lift through the crown of the head, chin parallel to the floor, shoulders relaxed, arms alongside the body.
hold: Breathe calmly through the nose.
Notice the small balance adjustments without correcting them abruptly.
exit: Release the engagement in the legs and let the breath become free again.
Flow into the next pose or close your eyes for a moment.

cuesShort: Root down through the four corners of your feet.
Grow tall through the crown of your head.
Shoulders away from your ears, arms heavy.
Breathe into the space you've just created.

cuesDetailed.cue: Weight spread between heels and balls of the feet, arches slightly lifted.
Straight but not hyperextended; kneecaps facing forward.
Neutral: neither arched nor tucked, tailbone pointing to the floor.
Lower ribs stacked over the pelvis, sternum slightly open.
Shoulder blades sliding down the back, collarbones broad.
Long neck, ears aligned over the shoulders, gaze on the horizon.

montagne.breath: Slow nasal breathing; on the inhale the body lengthens, on the exhale it grounds.
commonMistakes: Weight in the heels or pelvis pushed forward: bring the weight back to the middle of the foot.
Over-arching to "stand up straight": soften the lower ribs.

benefitsDetailed.text: Retrains standing alignment and reveals habitual imbalances (more weight on one foot, one shoulder higher).
Builds stability and a sense of being well grounded, useful at the start of a session or in stressful times.
A lengthened torso and relaxed shoulders leave more room for the breath.

montagne.precautions: Accessible to almost everyone. With dizziness or low blood pressure, keep the eyes open and stand near a wall.
modifications: Feet hip-width apart for more stability.
Back against a wall to feel the alignment of head, shoulders and pelvis.
Block between the thighs to feel the legs engage.

audience.note: During pregnancy, take the feet wider apart.

guerrier-2.summary: A powerful, open standing pose with a wide stance and arms extended horizontally. It builds leg strength and endurance while opening the hips and chest. The gaze resting beyond the front hand brings a quality of calm focus.
guerrier-2.sanskritMeaning: Vīrabhadra: a warrior from Indian mythology; āsana: pose.

entry: From Mountain, step the feet wide apart (about one leg length).
Turn the front foot out 90° and the back foot slightly in; front heel in line with the arch of the back foot.
Inhale, raise the arms to shoulder height, palms facing down.
Exhale, bend the front knee until it is over the ankle.
Turn the head and rest your gaze beyond the front middle finger.
hold: Keep the torso centered between the legs, without leaning forward.
Press the outer edge of the back foot into the floor.
exit: Inhale, straighten the front leg.
Bring the feet back to parallel and switch sides.

cuesShort: Front knee over the ankle.
Long arms, shoulders down.
Outer edge of the back foot grounded.
Torso centered, gaze beyond the hand.

cuesDetailed.cue: Pointing straight ahead; weight through the heel and the base of the big toe.
Tracking toward the second or third toe, without collapsing inward.
Straight and active, thigh rotating slightly outward.
Open toward the long side of the mat, sacrum long.
Reaching in both directions at shoulder height, fingers active.
Turns without the torso following; long neck.

guerrier-2.breath: Full, steady breathing; let the exhale deepen the knee bend.
commonMistakes: Front knee going past the ankle or collapsing inward: widen the stance or reduce the bend.
Torso leaning toward the front leg: bring the shoulders back over the pelvis.
Shoulders creeping up: release the trapezius while keeping the arms active.

benefitsDetailed.text: Strengthens the thighs, glutes and calves, and builds muscular endurance through the hold.
Opens the hips and stretches the inner thighs and the groin of the front leg.
The steady gaze and stable arms develop calm, sustained attention.

therapeutic: Low energy or mental fatigue (energizing pose)
guerrier-2.precautions: With knee pain, reduce the bend and check alignment. With shoulder pain, keep the hands on the hips. With neck problems, look straight ahead rather than toward the hand.
modifications: Shorten the stance and reduce the knee bend.
Hands on the hips to ease the shoulders.
Chair under the front thigh to hold longer.

stretched: hip flexors of the back leg

enfant.summary: The quintessential resting pose: sitting on the heels, torso folded over the thighs, forehead on the floor. It gently lengthens the back, relaxes the shoulders and calms the breath. Students can return to it at any time during class to recover, which makes it a key pose to offer.

entry: Come to kneeling with the big toes touching.
Keep the knees together or take them as wide as the mat.
Exhale, sit back on the heels and lower the torso toward the thighs.
Rest the forehead on the floor (or on a block).
Extend the arms forward or rest them alongside the body, palms up.
hold: Let the weight of the pelvis sink toward the heels.
Feel the back widen with each inhale.
exit: Place the hands under the shoulders.
Slowly roll the torso up, vertebra by vertebra, head last.

cuesShort: Hips toward the heels.
Forehead resting, jaw soft.
Breathe into your back.
Come back here whenever you need to.

cuesDetailed.cue: Heavy, sinking toward the heels; cushion between hips and heels if needed.
Long and rounded, widening on the inhale.
Relaxed; arms alongside the body for complete rest.
Forehead resting, neck free, no pressure on the eyes.

enfant.breath: Slow breathing into the back ribs and lower back; let the exhale lengthen.
commonMistakes: Hips far from the heels: slide a cushion in to allow release.
Forehead not reaching the floor: use a block rather than straining the neck.

benefitsDetailed.text: Calms the nervous system and invites turning inward, useful after effort or at the end of a session.
Gently lengthens the spine and releases the lower back.
Compressing the belly directs the breath into the back and encourages slow breathing.

enfant.precautions: Adapt for knee or ankle injuries (cushions, blanket under the ankles). During pregnancy, take the knees wide to make room for the belly. Avoid staying head-down for long with eye pressure.
modifications: Knees wide, torso between the thighs (pregnancy, sensitive belly).
Cushion between the hips and heels.
Block or stacked fists under the forehead.

audience.note: Seniors: generous cushions under the hips and forehead.

stretched: muscles on top of the foot

pigeon.summary: A deep hip opener: front leg folded in front of you, back leg extended. It stretches the hip rotators and glutes on one side and the hip flexors on the other. Practiced with an upright torso it is active; with the torso folded forward it becomes a pose of letting go.
pigeon.sanskritMeaning: Eka: one; pāda: leg; kapota: pigeon.
pigeon.typicalHold: 8 to 15 breaths on each side, up to 3 minutes in the yin version

entry: From Downward Dog or tabletop, bring one knee forward behind the wrist on the same side.
Lower the front shin to the floor, foot toward the opposite wrist (more or less parallel to the front of the mat depending on your openness).
Extend the back leg, top of the foot on the floor.
Square the hips and let them sink; tuck a blanket under the front hip if it doesn't reach the floor.
Lengthen the torso on the inhale, then, if comfortable, fold forward onto the forearms or forehead.
hold: Keep the front foot active (flexed) to protect the knee.
Breathe into the hip without forcing.
exit: Bring the hands back under the shoulders and tuck the back toes.
Return to tabletop or Downward Dog and switch sides.

cuesShort: Front knee behind the wrist.
Front foot active, toes spread.
Hips square and sinking.
Breathe into the hip, without forcing.

cuesDetailed.cue: No pain; bring the foot closer to the pelvis if the knee pulls.
Flexed to stabilize the knee.
Both hip points facing forward; support under the front hip if needed.
Extended straight back from the hip, thigh rotating toward the floor.
Long before folding; in the forward fold, let the head rest.

pigeon.breath: Slow breathing; with each exhale, let the pelvis sink a few millimeters.
commonMistakes: Pelvis tipping onto the front hip: slide a blanket underneath.
Front knee pulling or hurting: close the shin angle or switch to Reclining Figure Four.
Back leg drifting outward: realign it behind the hip.

benefitsDetailed.text: Stretches the external rotators and glutes of the front leg, often tight in runners and people who sit for long periods.
Stretches the hip flexors of the back leg.
In the forward-folding version, it invites patience and release, often associated with the hips in yoga traditions.

therapeutic: Glute and piriformis tension (without acute sciatic pain)
pigeon.precautions: Avoid with a knee or hip injury or replacement, and adapt for sacroiliac pain. Any knee pain is a signal to stop: offer Reclining Figure Four instead.
modifications: Blanket or block under the front hip.
Front shin closer to the pelvis.
Lying-on-the-back version (Figure Four) to ease the knees.
Bolster under the torso in the forward-folding version.

audience.note: Pregnancy: keep the torso upright, support under the hip.

chien-tete-en-bas.summary: An iconic inverted-V pose, hands and feet on the floor, hips high. It stretches the entire back body, strengthens the arms and shoulders, and serves as a transition and active rest in sequences. A mild inversion, it places the head below the heart and revitalizes.
chien-tete-en-bas.sanskritMeaning: Adho: downward; mukha: face; śvāna: dog.
chien-tete-en-bas.typicalHold: 5 breaths in a flow, up to 1 minute as a hold

entry: Come to tabletop, hands slightly in front of the shoulders, fingers spread.
Tuck the toes.
Exhale, lift the knees and send the hips up and back.
Keep the knees bent at first to lengthen the back, then gradually straighten the legs.
Let the head hang between the arms, ears in line with the arms.
hold: Press the floor away with your hands to move the hips away from the wrists.
Let the heels sink toward the floor without forcing.
exit: Lower the knees and sit back on the heels into Child's Pose.
Or walk the feet to the hands into Standing Forward Fold.

cuesShort: Push the floor away, hips high.
Soft knees, long back.
Heels toward the floor, no forcing.
Neck relaxed between the arms.

cuesDetailed.cue: Fingers spread, pressing through the base of the index finger and thumb to ease the wrist.
Straight, elbow creases facing each other.
Broad, shoulder blades spreading and sliding toward the hips.
Long from head to tailbone; a long back takes priority over straight legs.
Sit bones reaching up and back.
Thighs pressing back, heels sinking.

chien-tete-en-bas.breath: Slow, deep breathing; with each exhale, lengthen the spine a little more.
commonMistakes: Rounded back to straighten the legs: bend the knees.
Shoulders hunched to the ears: push the floor away and widen the upper back.
Weight in the wrists: shift the weight back toward the legs.
Feet too close to the hands: lengthen the pose.

benefitsDetailed.text: Stretches the hamstrings, calves, back and shoulders in a single pose.
Strengthens the arms, shoulders and the abdominal wall that stabilizes the trunk.
The mild inversion supports venous return and brings a sense of revitalization.

chien-tete-en-bas.precautions: Avoid or adapt with carpal tunnel syndrome, shoulder injury, uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma, or in late pregnancy. Come out of the pose if you feel dizzy or get a headache.
modifications: Hands on blocks or a chair to ease the wrists and shoulders.
Dolphin version, on the forearms, if the wrists hurt.

audience.note: Pregnancy: short hold, hands on a chair in the third trimester.
